title: Cap'n Proto (zero-copy serialization)
summary: Cap'n Proto is a zero-copy serialization format by the creator of Protocol Buffers. A Cap'n Proto message: segment table (number of segments + segment sizes), then segments (each a sequence of 64-bit words). Pointers (struct, list, text, data) are 64-bit values with type, offset, and size. Structs are fixed-size with a data section and pointer section. Lists can be of primitives, pointers, or structs.

structure.meaning: Size of each segment in 8-byte words.
64-bit words: struct pointers, list pointers, text/data pointers, and primitive values.
Type (2 bits) + offset (30 bits) + data size (16 bits) + pointer count (16 bits).
Type (2 bits) + offset (30 bits) + element size (3 bits) + element count (29 bits).

notes: Cap'n Proto requires no parsing: the serialized bytes ARE the in-memory representation.
Built-in RPC protocol with promise pipelining.
Cap'n Proto is used by Cloudflare (Workers), Sandstorm, and high-performance systems.
Unlike FlatBuffers, Cap'n Proto supports complex types (unions, generics) and RPC.
